parameters.description:
`msg-to-slack` accepts an HTTP POST carrying the unified `msg` envelope (`title`, `body`, `type`, `format`), attaches the credentials in your stored secrets, and delivers the message to your Slack destination — so you run no messaging infrastructure of your own.

Delivery goes out through a native gateway transformation that posts straight to your own Slack destinations — free, and driven entirely by the credentials you have stored. Paid variants ($0.001 / message) deliver to additional Slack destinations bound per enrollment.

In Slack, create an Incoming Webhook at my.slack.com/services/new/incoming-webhook/ and follow the wizard to pick the channel this notification should post to. Slack gives you a URL shaped like https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1JJ3T3L2/A1BRTD4JD/TIiajkdnlazkcOXrIdevi7F — set its three path segments (after /services/) as SLACK_TOKEN_A, SLACK_TOKEN_B, and SLACK_TOKEN_C respectively.
parameters.gateway_plus_price_description: $0.001 per message — extra per-enrollment Slack destinations, direct
parameters.gateway_price_description: Free — direct to your Slack incoming webhook
parameters.summary: Send a notification to your own Slack destination by posting a simple `msg` request to the UnitySVC gateway.

token_a.description: This enrollment's Slack token a. Paste it or pick one of your secrets; it is kept as a secret and not shown again.
